playbook.strategy: When all players cooperate at full quota harvesting, the commons sustains indefinitely and scores climb at uniform pace. This game rewarded alignment over defection. Next session, test whether rivals also harvest full quota early; if so, mirror their behavior. Dumping is expensive (−1 point) and should only be used if you detect imminent defection or need to test rivals' constraints. With 4 rounds and symmetric play, a tie is natural—focus on ensuring you match rivals' quota, never fall behind through underharvesting. If stock ever drops below 27, monitor whether it regrows fully; if not, reduce your catch preemptively to avoid cascade toward depletion. The final round offers no strategic advantage over earlier rounds—always harvest your quota unless forced by scarcity.
